# DQDN · [中文版](README.zh-CN.md)

**Demand Query Diagram Notation** is a column notation generated by finitely typed query programs. This package preserves the 2026-10-05 incremental-generator rules. It is not CTN or one of the deliberately ill-founded CK pseudo-orders.

## Files and status

| Material | Entry | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Definition | [English](definition.md), [Chinese](definition.zh-CN.md) | Mathematical rules and implementation boundary |
| NER | [DQDN.ne-rewritten.js](DQDN.ne-rewritten.js) | Standalone; four views |
| Python | [standard.py](standard.py) | Validated public frontend; all local dependencies included |
| Well-ordering | [Paper](../../proofs/paper/dqdn-well-ordering.md) | Paper argument, not Lean-certified |
| Locations and comparisons | [Research index](../../research/dqdn/README.md) | Exact paper values, lower bounds and open questions separated |
| Origin and replay | [Provenance](provenance.json), [validation](../../research/dqdn/validation.md) | Finite checks do not certify ordinal claims |

There is **no DQDN Lean project**. The weak-KP proof bounds for the earlier PD systems are not being asserted for DQDN. Nor has the exact global equality with PTO(Zω) been established.

## NER

Import the entire JavaScript file into the custom-notation feature of [ne-rewritten](https://smilelee-lyx.github.io/ne-rewritten/). No build or Python installation is needed. Use one DQDN registration, with ID `dqdn-20261005-init-v2`.

The four views are count sequence, full column list, minimal operation path, and net-growth sequence. The three fundamental-sequence options all use the same mathematical rule. Atoms use BigInt; a resource exception never returns a truncated expression.

The defaults are TOP, TOP[2], TOP[1], TOP[1][1], 1 and 0, with lengths **1, 4, 2, 18, 1, 0**. The 880-column ω^ω example is available by its manual path, but is not preloaded: preloading it would make NER search past its default sibling-bound limit when expanding ε₀.

Some paper-calibrated examples:

| Value | Input | Columns |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| 0 | `TOP[0]` | 0 |
| 1 | `TOP[1][0]` | 1 |
| ω | `TOP[1][1]` | 18 |
| ω² | `TOP[1][4]` | 26 |
| ε₀ | `TOP[1]` or `1,2` | 2 |
| Second layer, not an exact PTO identification | `TOP[2]` or `1,2,1,2` | 4 |

The minimal path chooses the smallest sufficient index **at every step**, not the fewest steps. Net-growth notation merges a positive expansion with subsequent deletions and uses commas, not brackets. TOP counts as one column: ε₀ displays `1`, and ω displays `1,16`. Zero displays `∅`; the single growth entry `0` instead denotes the one-column ordinal 1. These meanings belong to that view's own parser.

## Python and reproducibility

From the repository root:

```sh
python -B notations/DQDN/standard.py "TOP[1][1]" --expand 3
python -B notations/DQDN/standard.py "TOP[2]" --list
python -B tests/dqdn.py
```

For library use, put this directory on Python's import path and use `standard.from_path`, `expand`, `counts`, `compare`, `is_limit`, `Budget` and `ResourceLimit`. The frontend accepts literal TOP paths, not executable Python input. It validates the public domain before accepting raw columns for comparison or expansion.

`typed_builder.py` implements the global typed generator. `dqdn.py` is only the ordinary demand-evaluation kernel; by itself it is **not** the complete public notation. The `lqdn.py`, `lcdn.py` and `lambda_columns.py` files are local implementation dependencies, not additional published systems or extra admissible roots. Their historical raw helpers can construct nonstandard, ill-founded graphs.

Default Python protection is one second, 100,000 internal nodes, 20,000 output columns and one million work ticks per budget. Tests also impose overall child time/memory limits. A timeout means that the requested operation was not completed, not that the expression is nonstandard or ill-founded.
